name: Robots.txt Generator
description: Build a valid robots.txt with one or more user-agent rule groups, allow/disallow paths, crawl-delay, and sitemap references — download it ready to upload.

faq.question: What does an empty Disallow line mean?
faq.answer: Disallow: with nothing after it means "block nothing" — that user-agent may crawl the entire site. It's the standard way to explicitly allow full access, rather than omitting the directive entirely.

faq.question: Does robots.txt stop a page from appearing in search results?
faq.answer: Not reliably. It asks crawlers not to fetch a path, but a URL that's linked to from elsewhere can still be indexed without ever being crawled — you'll sometimes see a listing with no description because of this. Use a noindex meta tag on the page itself if the goal is keeping it out of search results, or real access control if it needs to be actually private.

faq.question: Where does this file need to go?
faq.answer: robots.txt must be placed at the root of your domain (https://example.com/robots.txt) — search engines don't check subdirectories.
